messages:
sasha: quick follow-up to the prefetch cooldown RFC. i've prototyped an allocator-integrated approach that signals the runtime to defer non-critical prefetches and expand software coalescing when host IO queues are saturated.

ben: curious how this ties into the allocator's demotion/evict path. do you make prefetch decisions before demotion or after?

sasha: before demotion completes we already emit a hint (DEMOTE_PENDING) from allocator -> prefetch manager. when the hint is active we treat subsequent prefetch hints from that tenant as low priority. the idea is to avoid prefetching pages that are about to be demoted/evicted and causing immediate page-churn.

priya: can you show the config/contract? i'd like to see how ops can tune this per-pool.

sasha: sketch below. key additions: prefetch_cooldown policy, per-pool token bucket for emergency bypass, and an allocator hint enum added to the hint API.

```
# prefetch_cooldown config (defaults)
prefetch_cooldown:
  enabled: true
  policy: "adaptive"   # options: always, adaptive, never
  adaptive:
    base_delay_ms: 20
    max_delay_ms: 1500
    cooldown_inc: 1       # increments per conflicting hint
    decay_secs: 60
  coalesce:
    base_window_ms: 4
    max_window_ms: 80
    multiplier_on_cooldown: 3
  bypass:
    per_tenant_tokens: 5  # emergency bypass tokens
    replenish_interval_s: 60
allocator_hint_api:
  new_hint: DEMOTE_PENDING | HOT_ACCESS | PREFETCH_OPPORTUNITY
```

ben: nice. how does the adaptive policy decide increments? is it purely hint-count based or does it look at IO latency and queue depth?

sasha: both. we maintain a small sliding window of IO latency and queue depth from the host-level metrics. conflict events (demote pending + prefetch request) increment the conflict counter; high queue_depth or remote-tier-latency amplify the cooldown (i.e., we multiply cooldown_inc by a factor derived from normalized queue depth).

lee: sounds like a control loop. any stability concerns? we don't want oscillations where cooldowns flip on/off rapidly across tenants.

sasha: we add hysteresis by using an exponential decay on the conflict counter and by smoothing the queue-depth signal with an EWMA. we also cap rollout rate by limiting max change per-second so cooldown windows adapt slowly.

priya: what about fairness and noisy neighbors? if one tenant consumes all bypass tokens we could starve others.

sasha: bypass tokens are per-tenant and non-transferable. we also enforce a global fraction cap so no single-tenancy pool can use >20% of host bypass capacity. plus operator-level emergency policies can disable bypass on a per-pool basis.

ben: interaction with hardware/batcher? if the GPU driver/firmware already aggregates prefetch IOs, doubling up in software could increase latency.

sasha: agreed. runtime batcher will consume hints. when in cooldown, prefetch hints are downgraded to "low_priority_prefetch" which the batcher tries to fold into the next regular batch window rather than emitting immediate IO. if the driver coalesces, the low_priority flag is ignored and the driver controls actual IO timing.

priya: any risk to correctness? e.g., we delay prefetch for a page that is required mid-request and cause additional compute stalls.

sasha: we never defer critical-path prefetches. callers can mark prefetch as critical. also the per-tenant bypass tokens allow a short-circuit for latency-sensitive requests. default policy keeps generation latency as primary SLO.

devops: telemetry wishlist so we can tune in prod?

sasha: metrics I plan to add: pref.cold.defer_count{tenant,pool}, pref.cold.defer_duration_ms histogram, allocator.hint.demote_pending_count, host.io_queue_depth, host.remote_latency_ms p50/p99. also an alert if avg defer_duration_ms > 200ms across host.

lee: testing matrix? we should do unit, sim, and cluster e2e with slow-tier emulation.

sasha: test plan: unit tests for hint-state transitions and token behavior; a simulator that replays mixed-tenant traces with configurable remote-latency patterns; e2e using fio to emulate a slow NVMe tier and synthetic clients driving mixed request sizes. PR will include the simulation harness.

priya: rollout plan? prefer dedicated pool canary first.

sasha: rollout suggestion: staged canary: 1) internal-only dedicated pool (5% capacity) for 12h, monitor metrics; 2) expand to 10% across two hosts for 24h; 3) gradual global release. rollback triggers: p99 generation latency > +7% sustained for 15m, host fragmentation ratio increase > 8% vs baseline, or IO ops/sec drop > 10%.

devops: include a feature-flag gate and a prometheus-backed kill-switch so we can flip off adaptive policy instantly.

sasha: yes feature-flagged and operator opt-out at pool level.

infra-bot: ci/build #6012 success  diff includes prefactor changes + hint enum + unit tests.

ben: minor nit: rename multiplier_on_cooldown -> coalesce_multiplier to be clearer.

sasha: good call, will change in PR.

priya: also add a short doc blurb in runtime-designs explaining hint semantics so infra oncall understands the new signals.

sasha: will add docs + an ops runbook for how to interpret pref.* metrics during canary. thanks for the feedback, i'll open the PR and tag you both.

infra-bot: deploy-preview: https://ci.redwood/preview/6012

lee: :thumbsup: i'll help with the fio scenario and run the first canary.

sasha: awesome — thanks everyone.
